findings.defective_text: The same root answers itself at the row's own close: מִמֶּרְחָ֔ק (oshb:Isa.30.27, byte tier) is picked up by בֹּעֲרָ֖ה (oshb:Isa.30.33, byte tier), a root-level inclusio running the row's own length across two distinct attested spellings.
findings.byte_evidence: oshb:Isa.30.27 token 5 = מִמֶּרְחָ֔ק (byte tier, root rch-q, 'from far away'); oshb:Isa.30.33 token 20 = בֹּעֲרָ֖ה (byte tier, root b-'-r, 'burning'). The two share NO root, so the asserted root-level inclusio does not exist as spliced. The verse's actual b-'-r partner is the NEXT token, oshb:Isa.30.27 token 6 = בֹּעֵ֣ר (byte tier; byte sweep of that form: 1 verse, accent_stripped 2, skeleton 22) — a one-token word-index slip. Sentence is newly installed this wave (absent from the pre-apply corpus).
findings.proposed_cure: Replace the oshb:Isa.30.27 splice in that sentence with token 6, בֹּעֵ֣ר, so the inclusio is stated between the two attested b-'-r spellings it actually rests on.

findings.field: device_notes (byte-identical block installed on BOTH rows of the 5:19|5:20 seam pair)
findings.defective_text: Across this seam, the participle opening MT 5:19, הָאֹמְרִ֗ים (oshb:Isa.5.19, byte tier), and the participle opening MT 5:20, הָאֹמְרִ֥ים (oshb:Isa.5.20, byte tier), are accent-stripped-identical and differ only in accent at byte tier (sweep: 3 verses book-wide at accent-stripped tier, 4 at skeleton tier), both pointed forms byte-unique to their own verse.
findings.byte_evidence: TWO byte-checkable errors, both carried identically on both rows. (a) MT 5:20 does NOT open with the participle: oshb:Isa.5.20 token 1 = ה֣וֹי (byte tier) and the participle הָאֹמְרִ֥ים stands at token 2 — contradicted by these same rows' own boundary_rationale, which quotes MT 5:20 as opening ה֣וֹי הָאֹמְרִ֥ים לָרַ֛ע (byte tier). MT 5:19 alone opens with its participle (token 1). (b) 'both pointed forms byte-unique to their own verse' is false for the MT 5:20 form: הָאֹמְרִ֥ים stands byte-identical at oshb:Isa.42.17 token 7 (byte sweep: 2 verses). Only the MT 5:19 form הָאֹמְרִ֗ים is byte-unique (byte sweep: 1 verse). The two adjacent digits ARE correct: accent_stripped 3 verses (5:19, 5:20, 42:17), skeleton 4 verses (+65:5).
findings.proposed_cure: In the one shared block, restate MT 5:20's participle as verse-second after its hoy onset and replace the byte-unique claim with the true split — MT 5:19's form byte-unique (sweep: 1 verse), MT 5:20's form byte-shared with oshb:Isa.42.17 (sweep: 2 verses) — installing the identical wording on both rows in one edit.

findings.defective_text: the clause it introduces carries the standing כֹ֨ה אָמַ֧ר divine-frame formula (48 verses book-wide)
findings.byte_evidence: Skeleton sweep of the koh-amar formula = 48 verses book-wide, and that 48 INCLUDES the four royal-messenger sites oshb:Isa.36.4, oshb:Isa.36.14, oshb:Isa.36.16 and oshb:Isa.37.3 (all present in the sweep's hit list). The divine-frame count is 44, not 48. The toolkit hazard is explicit that a koh-amar digit must name whose frame it counts; here the prose names the frame ('divine-frame formula') and then supplies the blended total. Sentence newly installed this wave.
findings.proposed_cure: Change the parenthesis to name the counted object honestly — either '(the formula: sweep: 48 verses book-wide; 44 divine-frame, 4 royal-messenger)' or '(divine-frame sites: sweep: 44 verses)'.

findings.defective_text: the cohortative “אָשִׁ֤ירָה נָּא֙ לִֽידִידִ֔י שִׁירַ֥ת” (oshb:Isa.5.1, byte tier)  [representative of 73 sites]
findings.byte_evidence: Campaign law is explicit in both the toolkit and the author brief: curly double quotes are for verbatim WEB text with an in-field web: ref ONLY; everything else takes straight quotes. A programmatic scan of the three prose fields across all 223 rows finds curly-quoted HEBREW runs at 73 sites, ALL of them in part P02 (one further site in P18); 44 of the 73 are newly installed in this author wave, i.e. the repair re-emitted and extended the breach. This is invisible to Tier-0: check_web_quotes.py only inspects curly-quoted ENGLISH near web: refs, so the marker the WEB-quote gate depends on is being spent on oshb:-referenced Hebrew. Boss ledger contains no adjudication of this convention (no 'curly'/'quote convention' entry).
findings.proposed_cure: Re-quote every Hebrew run in part P02's prose fields with straight quotes in one mechanical pass, leaving curly quotes to WEB text with an in-field web: ref.

findings.repair_installed: P03-014 installed this wave; P06 sites re-emitted this wave (same sentences rewritten to change the ref prefix, register slip carried through)
findings.defective_text: P03-014: 'This unit spans the whole of chapter 12 (6 verses, verse_inventory.json), so confidence here is held at medium_low...'  |  P06-001/002/003/005/006: 'A setumah mark falls at oshb:Isa.21.17, the verse immediately preceding this row's own span (pmarks inventory, SAMEKH, single-witness corroboration, not a boundary driver).'
findings.byte_evidence: The register purge bars tool filenames and staged-file names/stems in ANY field. 'verse_inventory.json' is the staged file's literal filename and is newly installed in P03-014's device_notes; a programmatic filename scan over the whole corpus returns this as the only literal staged filename in row prose. 'pmarks' is the stem of the staged parashah inventory and stands in five P06 rows' device_notes, each of which the author rewrote this wave (web: -> oshb: ref-prefix change) without striking the stem. The same fact is stated register-clean elsewhere in the corpus: P02-009 writes '(13 verses, per the book's verse inventory)' and P09-001 writes '(9 verses, per the book's verse inventory)'. Related, same field family: P06-001 device_notes carries 'poetry_lines is 0 across 11 verses in the staged WEB extract' (staged-data field name; pre-existing, survived the wave).
findings.proposed_cure: Strike the staged names — 'verse_inventory.json' becomes 'per the book's verse inventory' (the phrasing already used in P02-009 and P09-001), 'pmarks inventory' becomes 'the parashah inventory', and 'poetry_lines ... in the staged WEB extract' becomes a plain layout statement.

findings.defective_text: P08-012: 'this catchword adds further, previously undisclosed corroboration rather than contesting either.'  |  P01-011: 'The row's own opening seam carries undisclosed cross-seam cohesion: ...' and 'The undisclosed link leaves a live rival unstated: ...'  |  P01-007: 'the primary undisclosed cohesion signal at 1:26|1:27'  |  P08-004/005/006: 'straddles the row's own front seam undisclosed' / 'crosses this row's rear seam undisclosed' / 'crosses this row's front seam undisclosed'.
findings.byte_evidence: Every one of these strings is absent from the pre-apply corpus and newly installed by this wave (diff of the five prose fields, all 223 rows). The author brief's register purge is categorical — no erratum narration, 'the repaired row reads as if written right the first time' — and 'previously undisclosed' (P08-012) is a temporal marker naming the row's own prior state; the bare 'undisclosed' sites are self-contradictory, since the sentence carrying the word IS the disclosure, and 'disclosed/undisclosed' is the campaign's own cross-seam-cohesion rule vocabulary. The same class runs on past my half at P11-007, P11-008, P11-013, P13-002, P15-004, P16-001, P16-008, P18-007, P18-008 (two of those, P13-002 and P16-008, carry the explicit 'until now'), so the cure should be swept, not spot-fixed.
findings.proposed_cure: Strike the status word — state the signal and its tier ('A catchword straddles this row's own front seam: ...') and let the sentence be the disclosure, sweeping the whole corpus rather than the six rows in this half.

findings.defective_text: the bare banner noun itself may not be swept for this claim — it is a short-token trap reaching 44 verses as a substring against 6 word-bound, neither set including this verse's own form.
findings.byte_evidence: Both digits are right: the bare banner noun's skeleton reaches 44 verses as a substring and 6 verses word-bound (oshb:Isa.5.26, 11.12, 13.2, 18.3, 33.23, 62.10). But this row's own verse oshb:Isa.11.10 IS a member of the 44-verse substring set — its token לְנֵ֣ס (byte tier, token 8) contains the two-consonant skeleton, which is precisely why the substring sweep hits it. Only the 6-verse word-bound set excludes it.
findings.proposed_cure: Narrow the exclusion to the set it holds for: '... against 6 word-bound, the word-bound set not including this verse's own prefixed form.'

findings.defective_text: that imperative pair stands verse-initial at exactly 3 verses book-wide ... [and] A second imperative pair opens verse-initially inside the span at דִּרְשׁ֨וּ מֵֽעַל סֵ֤פֶר יְהוָה֙ וּֽקְרָ֔אוּ ... standing verse-initial at exactly 2 verses book-wide
findings.byte_evidence: Both digits count the LEADING imperative alone, not the pair the sentence names. Verse-initial token-bound sweep of קִרְב֤וּ = 3 verses (oshb:Isa.34.1, 41.21, 48.16), but neither oshb:Isa.41.21 nor oshb:Isa.48.16 carries הַקְשִׁ֑יבוּ — the pair itself stands at 1 verse. Likewise verse-initial דִּרְשׁ֨וּ = 2 verses (oshb:Isa.34.16, 55.6), but oshb:Isa.55.6's second imperative is a different form from וּֽקְרָ֔אוּ, so that pair too stands at 1 verse. Sentence newly installed this wave.
findings.proposed_cure: Attach each digit to the object it counts — 'that opening imperative stands verse-initial at exactly 3 verses book-wide (the pair itself at 1)' and the same shape for the second site.

findings.defective_text: that feminine-imperative form reaches 3 verses book-wide (sweep: 3 verses)
findings.byte_evidence: The sentence quotes TWO imperatives from oshb:Isa.12.6 and then says 'that ... form' (singular). Neither reading yields 3 word-bound: צַהֲלִ֥י is token-exact at 2 verses (oshb:Isa.10.30, oshb:Isa.12.6) and וָרֹ֖נִּי at 1 verse. The digit 3 is the SUBSTRING skeleton count for the first imperative, whose third hit is the vav-prefixed וְצַהֲלִי֙ at oshb:Isa.54.1 token 7 — a different attested form. No tier and no word-bound/substring disclosure accompanies the digit, against the standing substring discipline the same row observes elsewhere.
findings.proposed_cure: Name the single form and its bound — e.g. 'צַהֲלִ֥י stands at 2 verses word-bound (sweep: 2 verses, skeleton, token-exact; 3 as a bare substring, the third hit vav-prefixed)'.
